To move from suspicion to a more certain diagnosis we need structural neuroimaging to look for frontal and/or anterior temporal atrophy (required for a probable bvFTD diagnosis) and to exclude alternative structural causes. MRI brain is the single most informative next test.

[TEST] MRI brain (structural MRI focusing on frontal and temporal lobes)
Normal

[THOUGHT] Structural MRI is normal, which doesn't exclude behavioural-variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) early on but makes the diagnosis less certain. The next most informative, efficient step is a brief cognitive screen focused on executive function and attention to document objective impairment consistent with a neurodegenerative syndrome. A MoCA will rapidly assess executive dysfunction typical of bvFTD and help distinguish neurodegeneration from primary psychiatric or substance-related causes.

[TEST] Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) screening test.
Normal

[THOUGHT] A normal structural MRI and normal MoCA do not exclude behavioural-variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD), which can be early and show normal MRI and brief cognitive screening. The most informative next test to distinguish bvFTD from psychiatric or reversible causes is functional brain imaging (FDG-PET or HMPAO-SPECT) to look for frontal/anterior temporal hypometabolism/hypoperfusion. I'll request an FDG-PET brain scan focused on frontal and anterior temporal regions.

[TEST] FDG-PET brain (functional imaging to assess frontal and anterior temporal metabolism)

Cognitive screening (MMSE 28/30, MoCA normal), normal neurological exam, and normal MRI and FDG-PET make structural or widespread metabolic disease less likely but do not exclude an early neurodegenerative frontal-predominant process. The clinical syndrome meets core behavioral features (disinhibition, apathy, loss of empathy) with relative sparing of memory/visuospatial skills — most consistent with behavioural-variant frontotemporal dementia in its early stage (meets criteria for possible bvFTD despite normal imaging and brief cognitive tests).

[DIAGNOSIS] Behavioural-variant frontotemporal dementia (possible bvFTD).
